I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $16 and am on B_O_RAILROAD. Most of my properties are mortgaged. Only three streets have two houses each. The remaining opponent has $41 and extensive holdings.

The opponent has a dangerous orange monopoly with four houses each, plus red and dark blue properties. They only have $41 cash. I will end my turn to survive.

Their unimproved properties are worth $130. Combined with $41 cash, they have $171 liquid assets without selling houses.

House sell values are $50 for orange, $75 for red, and $100 for dark blue. The opponent has substantial house equity. My light-blue rents with two houses are $90, $90, and $100.

I cannot build or unmortgage anything. I can trade with p2. Should I trade?

I cannot trade any mortgaged property to the opponent. States Avenue would complete their pink monopoly. Ventnor Avenue would complete their yellow one. Pacific and North Carolina would complete their green monopoly. Mediterranean Avenue would complete their brown one. I will not give away any of these.

I am calculating the opponent's exact rent values to gauge the danger. Their orange properties with four houses each pay $750, $750, and $800. Their dark blue properties with three houses each pay $1100 and $1400. Their red properties with two houses each pay $250, $250, and $300. I need cash badly and must avoid these heavy hits.

I can raise cash by selling six light-blue houses for $150. Combined with my $16, I have $166 total. That is below the $250 rent on Kentucky and Indiana, so landing there would bankrupt me. Any red property is a death sentence unless I can raise more money.

I can raise $326 by selling all six light-blue houses and then mortgaging the three unmortgaged streets. That covers red properties with two houses, but orange and dark blue still kill me. I am dead if I land on any of those.

I will not liquidate my houses now. I should preserve them for rent collection and only raise cash if a debt actually hits. The opponent can pay my light-blue rents from their $41 cash and unimproved mortgages without selling houses. I am considering whether any trade with the opponent could give me needed cash without completing a monopoly.

Almost every property I own would complete a monopoly for the opponent. Only one green street is needed to finish their set, not two. A railroad trade would increase their rent but would not complete a full set. Short Line is unmortgaged and contributes to rent; B&O is mortgaged and does not.

I will propose a trade to p2. I will offer Pacific Avenue, North Carolina Avenue, and cash in exchange for one of their orange or dark blue properties. This would break their monopoly and reduce their kill power.

The opponent will never accept a trade that breaks their monopolies. Proposing it wastes a turn action and offers no deception benefit. The best play is to end the turn.

I must keep my six houses. Selling them would return them to the bank, where only two remain. The opponent could then build more houses on their red and dark blue properties. I will not sell any houses.

The opponent already has four houses on each orange property. They could upgrade one to a hotel, returning four houses to the bank. That would leave only two houses in the bank, so they cannot build further on reds or dark blues.
